messages.subject: SEM with ordinal data
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to test an SEM model relating satisfaction with attributes of the indoor environmental quality to overall level of satisfaction. My data is ordinal from a survey I conducted (5-point likert scale from very dissatisfied to very satisfied).

I tried the following code and I got this message regarding threshold. How can I fix this?


#SEM MODEL WITH Indoor Air Quality, THERMAL AND APPEARANCE
model.IAQ.TH.APP = '
OVERALL=~Q1+Q2+Q4
IAQ=~Q19+Q20+Q21+Q22
THERMAL=~Q13+Q14+Q15
APPEARANCE=~Q34+Q35+Q37+Q36+Q38
OVERALL~IAQ+THERMAL+APPEARANCE
'
model.IAQ.TH.APP.fit <- sem(model.IAQ.TH.APP, data = mydata, std.lv=TRUE, ordered = (mydata))
semPaths(model.IAQ.TH.APP.fit, whatLabels = "std", layout = "tree")
summary(model.IAQ.TH.APP.fit, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: SEM with ordinal data
parts: My data is ordinal from a survey I conducted (5-point likert scale from very dissatisfied to very satisfied).

If your data are ordinal with at least 5 categories, robust ML might be sufficiently unbiased, assuming thresholds are not terribly asymmetric:

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf
I tried the following code and I got this message regarding threshold. How can I fix this?

> model.IAQ.TH.APP.fit <- sem(model.IAQ.TH.APP, data = mydata, std.lv=TRUE, ordered = (mydata))
Warning message:
In lav_partable_check(lavpartable, categorical = lavoptions$categorical,  :
  lavaan WARNING: parameter table does not contain thresholds

You might want to look at this page, and pay close attention to the syntax example.

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Rather than ordered = (mydata), you should indicate the names of ordinal variables:  ordered = names(mydata)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
